questions.prompt: In the vector [alpha, beta]^T, which entry belongs to |0>?
questions.explanation: The stated basis order is [|0>, |1>], so the first entry is the amplitude of |0>.

questions.prompt: How is a Z-basis probability obtained from an amplitude?

options.text: Multiply it by the shot count

questions.explanation: The Born rule uses squared magnitude, such as |i/2|^2 = 1/4.

questions.prompt: Which change is a global phase?

options.text: Multiply the whole state by i
Measure in X instead of Z

questions.explanation: A common phase factor multiplies the complete state and does not change isolated measurement probabilities.

questions.prompt: What do |+> and |-> share before an analyzing gate?

options.text: The same final result after every gate

questions.explanation: Both have 1/2 for 0 and 1 in Z, but their relative phases differ.

questions.prompt: For theta = pi/3, what is P(0) on the Bloch sphere?
What does changing phi mainly change for a pure qubit?

options.text: The relative phase around a latitude
The fact that a detector returns one bit

questions.explanation: Phi is the azimuthal angle and changes relative phase without changing direct Z probabilities at fixed theta.

questions.prompt: Where does a pure single-qubit state appear on the Bloch sphere?

options.text: At any point outside the sphere

questions.explanation: Pure states are represented by surface points. Mixed states lie inside the sphere.

questions.prompt: Why can one Z histogram fail to distinguish two qubit states?

options.text: Z measurement can hide relative phase

questions.explanation: Different relative phases can produce the same Z probabilities and become visible only in another basis or later circuit.
